requalification.kind: release requalification: previous stable release (baseline) against the 0.1.7 release tree (candidate)
requalification.note: Both releases contain the Q05 join change and the storage-scan change this evidence originally qualified; the pair measures every other engine change between the two releases, including segment format 7, the shared block cache, the vector decoding kernels and aggregation on the decoding workers.

scope: Warm-cache deterministic SF1 Q05 and four-query TPC-H comparison; not a general latency guarantee.

measurement.host_type: 16-vCPU cloud host (AMD Ryzen 9 9950X), 31 GiB RAM, /dev/kvm present, local docker daemon
measurement.note: 0.1.6 ran on 8-vCPU cloud hosts; compare arms only within this requalification. Every workload of this study ran on this one host, one after another.
measurement.pintail_placement: native process on the measurement host; the MySQL source ran in a container on the same host
measurement.host_fingerprint: not recorded: the TPC-H harnesses do not emit one
measurement.toolchain: rustc 1.97.1, release profile, dashboard prebuilt, one target directory per arm
measurement.background_work_wait: Before every replay the server was left until it used at most 0.05 s of CPU in each of three consecutive 10 s windows: 30 s for the baseline, 140 s for the candidate, whose merges rewrote the retained replica's fact table from 61 segments into 31.
measurement.competing_workload: None from this study. The host's management agents appeared in brief bursts; around the TPC-H replays two of about one logical CPU, both while a candidate server waited for its merges, none during a measured replay.
measurement.replica: One SF1 replica was created with the baseline executable and retained; both executables were then started on it in turn, baseline first. Setup and snapshot time are excluded.

target_repeat.note: The same fifteen-sample target repeated once on the same replica after the run of record.

four_query_candidate_repeat.note: Candidate replayed again on the retained replica after the 20M pair; all answers exact.

four_query_profile.note: The candidate read the replica after its own merges (31 segments, format 7). Block counters are not comparable across the versions: on the unmerged second replica the candidate reports 1,684 of 1,684 blocks for the 61 segments the baseline reports as 2,526 of 2,526. Not established what each counts.

layout_control.reason: The candidate's merges rewrote the retained replica, so the retained pair differs in layout. A second replica, built by the baseline from a fresh source with the same generator and seed, was copied three ways before any candidate touched it.
layout_control.baseline_on_candidate_written_replica: refused: the fact table failed to load with "unsupported format version" (segment format 7), as the 0.1.7 downgrade note states
layout_control.finding: The candidate is faster on every query with merges off, on the baseline's own 61-segment layout; the speedup comes from execution, not from the rewritten layout.

remaining_qualification.20m_regression: None: every candidate run is faster than every baseline run on all eight engine-track queries (pooled medians -75% to -91%) and on the memo track.
remaining_qualification.tpch_regression: None: all four TPC-H queries are faster in the candidate on both replicas.
